questions.stem: Which pattern best supports further evaluation for ADHD rather than a brief or single-setting attention problem?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Inattention has persisted for 8 months at school, but similar symptoms are not reported at home, with relatives, or during other activities.","B":"Inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity has persisted for at least 6 months, occurs in two or more settings, and impairs daily functioning.","C":"Symptoms occur at home and school and interfere with functioning, but they have been present for about 6 weeks following a major family disruption.","D":"Similar behaviors are reported at home and school for more than 6 months, but functioning and development remain age-appropriate despite the behaviors."}}
questions.rationale: ADHD diagnosis requires a persistent developmentally inappropriate pattern that causes impairment and occurs in more than one setting. Option B is correct because it includes at least 6 months of symptoms, two or more settings, and functional impairment. Option A is limited to one setting. Option C has lasted only about 6 weeks and follows a major disruption that may better explain the behavior. Option D lacks impairment despite persistent behaviors.
questions.source_name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Clinical Care of ADHD in Children
questions.source_detail: CDC clinical guidance updated June 1, 2026 states ADHD symptoms must persist at least 6 months, occur in two or more settings, and interfere with or reduce the quality of functioning.

questions.stem: A client receives naloxone for respiratory depression after a long-acting opioid and initially improves. Which nursing action is most important next?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue surveillance because the duration of many opioids exceeds naloxone's duration, so respiratory or CNS depression can recur after initial improvement.","B":"Stop close monitoring after sustained awakening for a short observation because recurrent respiratory depression is unlikely once normal conversation returns.","C":"Withhold additional naloxone if respiratory depression returns because repeat doses are not useful after the client has responded to an initial dose.","D":"Monitor mainly for opioid withdrawal rather than recurrent respiratory depression because naloxone's antagonist effect lasts longer than most opioids."}}
questions.rationale: Naloxone may wear off before the opioid does, so respiratory or CNS depression can recur after initial improvement. Option A is correct because continued surveillance is required and repeat naloxone may be needed. Option B stops monitoring too early. Option C incorrectly withholds repeat naloxone when recurrent respiratory depression occurs. Option D reverses the duration relationship between naloxone and many opioids.
questions.source_name: DailyMed / FDA Label — NARCAN (naloxone hydrochloride) nasal spray
questions.source_detail: Current NARCAN prescribing information states that the duration of most opioids may exceed naloxone's duration, so respiratory or CNS depression can recur after initial improvement and continued surveillance with repeat doses as needed is required.

questions.stem: A client asks how buprenorphine helps treat opioid use disorder. Which explanation is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Buprenorphine is a full opioid agonist comparable with methadone or heroin, so its respiratory and overdose effects are similar to full agonists.","B":"Buprenorphine is an opioid antagonist without agonist activity, so it treats opioid use disorder primarily by blocking opioid receptors.","C":"Buprenorphine is a partial opioid agonist that reduces withdrawal and cravings and has a safer overdose profile than full opioid agonists.","D":"Buprenorphine is a partial opioid agonist that generally increases withdrawal and cravings, so it is used mainly after recovery is already complete."}}
questions.rationale: Buprenorphine is a partial opioid agonist used for opioid use disorder. Option C is correct because it reduces withdrawal and cravings and has a safer overdose profile than full agonists, although overdose remains possible. Option A incorrectly calls it a full agonist. Option B incorrectly calls it a pure antagonist. Option D reverses its therapeutic effect by claiming it generally increases withdrawal and cravings.
questions.source_name: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration — Buprenorphine
questions.source_detail: SAMHSA guidance updated in 2026 describes buprenorphine as a partial opioid agonist that diminishes withdrawal symptoms and cravings, increases safety in overdose, and lowers misuse potential compared with full agonists.

questions.stem: A client taking methadone is prescribed another medication that can prolong the QT interval. Which concern is most important?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Methadone's main cardiac concern is sinus bradycardia rather than QT prolongation, so adding another QT-prolonging medication does not increase conduction risk.","B":"Methadone can prolong the QT interval and has been associated with torsades de pointes, so another drug affecting cardiac conduction adds arrhythmia risk.","C":"Methadone-related QT effects occur mainly after parenteral administration, so oral maintenance therapy has little relevance when another QT-prolonging drug is added.","D":"Methadone tends to shorten ventricular repolarization, so a second QT-prolonging medication is unlikely to create an additive cardiac-conduction concern."}}
questions.rationale: Methadone can prolong the QT interval and has been associated with torsades de pointes. Option B is correct because another medication affecting cardiac conduction can add risk and warrants attention. Option A substitutes sinus bradycardia as the principal concern. Option C incorrectly limits QT effects to parenteral use. Option D incorrectly states that methadone shortens ventricular repolarization.
questions.source_name: DailyMed / FDA Label — METHADOSE (methadone hydrochloride)
questions.source_detail: METHADOSE prescribing information revised April 2026 warns of life-threatening QT prolongation and torsades de pointes and advises close monitoring in patients with risk factors or medications affecting cardiac conduction.

questions.stem: A client starting disulfiram asks what products should be avoided. Which teaching is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Avoid beverage alcohol, but sauces and cough preparations do not require checking because alcohol in these products does not trigger the disulfiram reaction.","B":"Avoid alcohol and hidden sources such as sauces, vinegars, or cough preparations because alcohol exposure can trigger a serious disulfiram reaction.","C":"Use alcohol-containing topical products freely because disulfiram reactions require swallowing alcohol rather than skin or mucosal exposure.","D":"Resume alcohol 24 hours after the last disulfiram dose because the interaction risk is considered resolved by the following day of treatment."}}
questions.rationale: Disulfiram can produce a serious reaction with alcohol, including alcohol hidden in sauces, vinegars, cough preparations, and some topical products. Option B is correct. Option A incorrectly exempts hidden alcohol sources. Option C incorrectly assumes topical alcohol cannot trigger a reaction. Option D is unsafe because labeling warns that alcohol reactions may occur for up to 14 days after the last disulfiram dose.
questions.source_name: DailyMed / FDA Label — Disulfiram
questions.source_detail: Current DailyMed disulfiram labeling warns patients to avoid alcohol in disguised forms such as sauces, vinegars, cough mixtures, aftershave lotions, and back rubs and notes that reactions may occur up to 14 days after disulfiram.

questions.stem: A client taking lithium learns that she is in the first trimester of pregnancy and asks about fetal risk. Which teaching is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"First-trimester lithium has a potential cardiac-malformation risk, including a historical Ebstein signal; prompt prescriber review is appropriate now.","B":"First-trimester lithium exposure is expected to cause Ebstein anomaly in most exposed pregnancies, making the fetal outcome predictable from exposure alone.","C":"First-trimester lithium is considered unrelated to cardiac development, so pregnancy review can focus primarily on late neonatal medication effects.","D":"Lithium-related fetal risk is limited to late pregnancy, so first-trimester exposure does not warrant discussion of possible cardiac malformations."}}
questions.rationale: Current lithium labeling describes a historical first-trimester signal for cardiovascular malformations, especially Ebstein anomaly, while later studies suggest any increased cardiac-malformation risk is likely small and the data are insufficient to establish a drug-associated risk. Option A is the best answer because it accurately communicates potential risk and the need for prompt prescriber review. Option B greatly overstates certainty. Option C denies the cardiac-development concern. Option D incorrectly limits fetal risk discussion to late pregnancy.
questions.source_name: DailyMed / FDA Label — Lithium Carbonate
questions.source_detail: Current lithium labeling states that early first-trimester reports suggested increased cardiovascular malformations, especially Ebstein anomaly; subsequent studies suggest any increased cardiac-malformation risk is likely small and available data are insufficient to establish a drug-associated risk.

questions.stem: A client of childbearing potential taking valproate asks why pregnancy planning is important. Which explanation is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Valproate can cause fetal neural tube defects and lower offspring IQ; effective contraception and pregnancy counseling are important during treatment.","B":"Valproate fetal risk is concentrated late in pregnancy, so exposure around conception carries little concern for neural-tube or structural malformations.","C":"Folic acid supplementation is sufficient to remove the medication-related neural-tube risk, so valproate can be used without additional pregnancy counseling.","D":"Valproate may cause minor reversible neonatal effects, but current labeling does not associate in-utero exposure with cognitive or structural harm."}}
questions.rationale: Valproate exposure in pregnancy is associated with major congenital malformations including neural tube defects and with decreased IQ and neurodevelopmental disorders. Option A is correct and appropriately emphasizes contraception and pregnancy counseling. Option B incorrectly shifts risk away from conception and early pregnancy. Option C overstates folic acid as eliminating medication-related risk. Option D incorrectly minimizes structural and cognitive risks.
questions.source_name: DailyMed / FDA Label — Divalproex Sodium
questions.source_detail: Current divalproex labeling revised in 2026 warns of fetal congenital malformations including neural tube defects, decreased IQ, and neurodevelopmental disorders and advises effective contraception for women of childbearing potential when treatment is necessary.

questions.stem: A client taking lisinopril reports a newly confirmed pregnancy. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue lisinopril into the second trimester because the most important fetal toxicity occurs later and early pregnancy exposure does not require prompt review.","B":"Notify the prescriber promptly; when pregnancy is detected, lisinopril should be discontinued as soon as possible and treatment should be reassessed today.","C":"Continue lisinopril if blood pressure is controlled because stable maternal pressure prevents the fetal renal effects associated with this medication class.","D":"Reduce the lisinopril dose and continue it through pregnancy because lower exposure removes the fetal toxicity associated with renin-angiotensin blockade."}}
questions.rationale: Lisinopril carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity, and current labeling says to discontinue it as soon as pregnancy is detected and reassess therapy. Option B is correct. Option A delays review despite confirmed pregnancy. Option C incorrectly assumes controlled maternal blood pressure eliminates fetal toxicity. Option D incorrectly assumes dose reduction removes the risk of renin-angiotensin system blockade.
questions.source_name: DailyMed / FDA Label — Lisinopril
questions.source_detail: Current lisinopril labeling updated in 2026 carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity and directs clinicians to discontinue lisinopril as soon as pregnancy is detected because renin-angiotensin system drugs can injure or kill the developing fetus.

questions.stem: Soon after labor epidural placement, the fetal heart tracing develops late decelerations. Which maternal assessment should the nurse prioritize?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Assess maternal blood pressure because epidural anesthesia can cause hypotension, reduce uteroplacental perfusion, and contribute to fetal decelerations.","B":"Assess maternal temperature because acute fever is the characteristic immediate hemodynamic effect of epidural anesthesia that explains fetal decelerations.","C":"Assess maternal glucose because epidural anesthesia commonly causes abrupt hyperglycemia that directly reduces uteroplacental perfusion after placement.","D":"Assess for maternal hypertension because epidural anesthesia typically increases systemic vascular resistance enough to produce fetal decelerations."}}
questions.rationale: Epidural anesthesia can cause maternal hypotension, which can reduce uteroplacental perfusion and contribute to fetal late decelerations. Option A is correct and prioritizes blood-pressure assessment. Option B incorrectly identifies fever as the characteristic immediate hemodynamic effect. Option C incorrectly prioritizes hyperglycemia. Option D reverses the usual hemodynamic concern by expecting hypertension.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf / Open RN — Nursing Health Promotion: Labor & Delivery Care
questions.source_detail: Open RN Nursing Health Promotion (2025) identifies maternal hypotension as a cause requiring correction when late decelerations reflect uteroplacental insufficiency; epidural anesthesia is a recognized cause of maternal hypotension requiring blood-pressure and fetal monitoring.

questions.stem: A client receiving a high-dose sodium nitroprusside infusion develops unexplained metabolic acidosis, confusion, and clinical deterioration. Which toxicity should the nurse suspect?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Suspect cyanide toxicity because nitroprusside can generate cyanide faster than the body can eliminate it at higher infusion rates or sufficient exposure.","B":"Suspect thiocyanate toxicity as the immediate high-rate effect because cyanide generation remains below detoxification capacity even at higher infusion rates.","C":"Suspect methemoglobinemia as the primary early high-rate toxicity because clinically important cyanide accumulation is not associated with nitroprusside.","D":"Suspect rebound hypertension from the infusion because nitroprusside generally raises vascular resistance when administered at higher infusion rates."}}
questions.rationale: Sodium nitroprusside metabolism generates cyanide, and higher infusion rates or sufficient exposure can exceed the body's detoxification capacity. Option A is correct, especially with metabolic acidosis, confusion, and deterioration. Option B confuses acute cyanide risk with thiocyanate toxicity, which is a separate metabolite concern. Option C incorrectly makes methemoglobinemia the primary high-rate toxicity. Option D incorrectly describes rebound hypertension as the toxicity pattern.
questions.source_name: DailyMed / FDA Label — Sodium Nitroprusside Injection
questions.source_detail: DailyMed labeling updated November 17, 2025 warns that sodium nitroprusside generates dose-related cyanide that can become toxic or lethal; cyanide toxicity can present with metabolic acidosis, confusion, and clinical deterioration.

questions.stem: A client taking isotretinoin reports new depressive symptoms and a marked mood change. Which instruction is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Attribute the mood change to acne-related stress first and delay medication review unless more severe psychiatric symptoms develop during treatment.","B":"Stop isotretinoin and promptly contact the prescriber about the new mood symptoms because current labeling warns about depression and other psychiatric disorders.","C":"Reassure the client and continue routine follow-up because new depressive symptoms during isotretinoin treatment rarely require prompt evaluation.","D":"Schedule discussion at the next routine visit rather than reporting the mood change promptly because psychiatric assessment can wait until symptoms persist longer."}}
questions.rationale: Current isotretinoin labeling warns about depression, mood disturbance, psychosis, suicidality, and aggressive behavior. Option B is correct because new depressive symptoms should prompt immediate discontinuation of isotretinoin and prompt contact with the prescriber; further evaluation may be needed. Option A delays medication review. Option C minimizes a labeled psychiatric warning. Option D postpones assessment until a later visit despite new symptoms.
questions.source_name: DailyMed / FDA Label — Isotretinoin Capsules
questions.source_detail: Isotretinoin prescribing information revised July 2026 warns about depression and other psychiatric disorders and instructs patients who develop depression or mood disturbance to stop isotretinoin and promptly contact the prescriber; further evaluation may be necessary.

questions.stem: During electrosurgery, why should local surgical-smoke evacuation remain active whenever smoke-producing energy is being used?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It primarily lowers room temperature by removing heat produced by electrosurgical equipment and other energy devices positioned near the sterile field.","B":"It primarily shortens operative time by removing visible vapor so the surgeon can complete tissue cutting and coagulation more rapidly during surgery.","C":"It reduces staff exposure to airborne surgical-smoke contaminants by capturing hazardous particles and gases close to the point where they are generated.","D":"It mainly prevents electrical interference with monitors by drawing ionized air away from cables and other equipment located around the procedure room area."}}
questions.rationale: NIOSH recommends local exhaust controls for laser/electrosurgical smoke and states that the smoke evacuator should be active whenever airborne particles are produced. Option C matches that purpose. The other options describe effects that are not the primary function of smoke evacuation.
questions.source_name: CDC/NIOSH — Control of Smoke From Laser/Electric Surgical Procedures
questions.source_detail: NIOSH identifies toxic gases, vapors, bioaerosols and cellular material in surgical smoke and recommends local exhaust ventilation with the smoke evacuator active whenever airborne particles are produced.

questions.stem: During a surgical laser procedure, which eye protection is appropriate for personnel exposed to the laser hazard?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Dark-tinted sunglasses are adequate if the wearer avoids looking directly at the beam and remains several feet from the laser during activation.","B":"Standard splash goggles are adequate because they block reflected laser energy regardless of the wavelength, power setting, or required optical density.","C":"Laser protective eyewear selected for the specific wavelength and adequate optical density should be worn as required within the controlled laser area.","D":"Eye protection is required only for the laser operator because scattered or reflected laser energy does not pose a significant hazard to other room staff."}}
questions.rationale: OSHA laser-safety guidance requires protective eyewear that provides adequate protection for the specific wavelength and optical density involved. Option C is correct. Ordinary sunglasses or splash goggles are not substitutes, and laser hazards are not limited to the operator.
questions.source_name: OSHA — Hospitals eTool: Surgical Suite, Laser Hazards
questions.source_detail: OSHA states that laser protective eyewear must provide adequate protection against the specific laser wavelengths being used and must be marked with optical density and wavelength.

questions.stem: Before an MRI examination, which safety action remains essential even when the client is calm and has no anxiety about the scan?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Screen the client and items entering the MR environment for ferromagnetic objects and verify the MR safety status of implanted medical devices.","B":"Skip device screening when the client has undergone previous imaging because prior tolerance establishes that every implant remains MR safe.","C":"Allow jewelry and other metallic objects to remain in place if they are small because projectile risk is limited to large metal equipment.","D":"Assume an implanted device is safe unless the client reports discomfort because device heating or malfunction can be detected after scanning begins."}}
questions.rationale: MRI safety is unrelated to whether the client feels anxious. FDA guidance emphasizes careful screening for projectile hazards and verification of implanted-device MR safety. Option A is correct; unknown devices should not simply be assumed safe.
questions.source_name: U.S. FDA — MRI Benefits and Risks
questions.source_detail: FDA states that careful screening of people and objects entering the MR environment is critical and that implanted devices must be positively identified as MR Safe or MR Conditional before MRI.

questions.stem: A hospital tracks hand-hygiene opportunities and completed hand-hygiene actions, then gives the results to staff. What is the primary purpose?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"To replace infection-prevention education with a numerical score that becomes the only measure used to evaluate whether staff provide safe clinical care.","B":"To identify individual staff for discipline rather than examine system gaps, barriers, adherence patterns, or infection-prevention outcomes across the unit.","C":"To monitor adherence, identify improvement opportunities, and provide feedback supporting better infection-prevention performance across the facility team.","D":"To document compliance without using the findings to change practice because monitoring data should remain separate from quality-improvement activities."}}
questions.rationale: CDC core infection-prevention practices call for monitoring adherence and providing prompt, regular feedback. Option C correctly describes performance monitoring as a quality-improvement tool. The other options incorrectly make monitoring punitive, isolated, or disconnected from improvement.
questions.source_name: CDC — Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices
questions.source_detail: CDC recommends identifying and monitoring adherence to infection-prevention practices and providing prompt, regular feedback on adherence and related outcomes.

questions.stem: A facility enters crisis-capacity PPE operations during a severe shortage. Which statement best describes crisis-capacity strategies?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"They are routine PPE practices that should continue after normal supply recovers because crisis strategies are the preferred long-term approach for conserving available stock.","B":"They remove the need for required PPE during direct patient care whenever a facility formally declares that its available protective supplies are severely limited.","C":"They apply only to nonclinical support staff, while clinicians must continue conventional PPE practices even when required protective supplies are unavailable.","D":"They are temporary measures for severe shortages when conventional and contingency strategies cannot meet demand, with standard practice restored as supply improves."}}
questions.rationale: CDC/NIOSH describes crisis-capacity strategies as measures used during known shortages when supply cannot meet utilization, not as routine practice. Option D is correct. Crisis capacity does not make PPE optional and should be discontinued as supply conditions improve.
questions.source_name: CDC/NIOSH — Conserving Personal Protective Equipment During Supply Shortages
questions.source_detail: CDC/NIOSH distinguishes conventional, contingency and crisis-capacity strategies and describes crisis capacity as temporary use during known shortages when supply cannot meet utilization.

questions.stem: During START mass-casualty triage, what does a red triage tag indicate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The person requires immediate intervention and transport because an airway, breathing, circulation, or other time-critical problem threatens survival.","B":"The person has minor injuries and can safely wait for treatment because the condition is unlikely to deteriorate significantly during the next several days.","C":"The person has serious injuries but treatment and transport can be delayed because major deterioration is not expected during the next several hours.","D":"The person is classified as expectant because survival is unlikely with available resources, so immediate transport is not the initial priority."}}
questions.rationale: The HHS CHEMM START algorithm defines red as Immediate: the person can be helped by immediate intervention and transport and needs medical attention within minutes. Green is minor, yellow delayed, and black expectant.
questions.source_name: HHS CHEMM — START Adult Triage Algorithm
questions.source_detail: The federal CHEMM START triage reference identifies Red as Immediate, requiring medical attention within minutes for survival and including airway, breathing, or circulation compromise.

questions.stem: A client is placed on Contact Precautions. Which PPE should be readily available for staff entering for interactions involving the client or environment?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Only a surgical mask, because Contact Precautions rely on respiratory source control rather than barriers for hands and clothing.","B":"Only eye protection, because environmental contact does not require gloves or gowns when the client is in a private patient room.","C":"Gloves and a gown appropriate to the anticipated contact, in addition to Standard Precautions and any task-specific PPE that is indicated.","D":"No dedicated PPE, because hand hygiene alone replaces gowns and gloves whenever the infectious agent is spread by direct or indirect contact."}}
questions.rationale: CDC Contact Precautions guidance calls for gloves and gown for interactions that may involve contact with the patient or the patient environment. Option C is correct. Masks or eye protection may be added when indicated by Standard Precautions, but they do not replace gown and gloves for Contact Precautions.
questions.source_name: CDC — Transmission-Based Precautions
questions.source_detail: CDC states that Contact Precautions include appropriate PPE, including gloves and gown, for interactions that may involve contact with the patient or the patient environment.

questions.stem: A hospitalized client requires Airborne Precautions. Which room feature is preferred for appropriate inpatient placement?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"An airborne infection isolation room maintained at negative pressure relative to adjacent areas so room air does not flow outward into the corridor.","B":"A standard private room maintained at positive pressure so filtered room air is pushed outward and prevents surrounding corridor air from entering that space.","C":"A semiprivate room with ordinary ventilation because closing its door provides the same containment as a dedicated airborne isolation room.","D":"Any available room without pressure monitoring because a fit-tested respirator eliminates the need for airborne-infection engineering controls."}}
questions.rationale: CDC recommends placement of patients requiring Airborne Precautions in an AIIR. An AIIR is maintained at negative pressure so air flows into the room rather than out to adjacent spaces. Positive-pressure protective environments serve a different purpose.
questions.source_name: CDC — Airborne Infection Isolation Room Guidance
questions.source_detail: CDC defines an AIIR as a single-occupancy room with negative pressure relative to surrounding areas and recommends an AIIR for patients requiring Airborne Precautions.

questions.stem: A medical-surgical nurse is floated to a pediatric ICU where the nurse has not previously practiced. What is the safest assignment approach?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Assign the most complex patient first because prior hospital experience and an active RN license establish competency for an unfamiliar specialty population.","B":"Give a full independent assignment without unit support because a current RN license and medical-surgical experience establish competence for every specialty.","C":"Require the usual pediatric ICU workload before discussing limitations because immediate staffing needs take priority over specialty competency.","D":"Match the assignment to verified knowledge and skills, provide appropriate orientation or training, and modify the workload or provide support as needed."}}
questions.rationale: ANA staffing guidance says nurses should assess whether they have expertise for a float population and whether cross-training, a buddy system, supervision, or assignment modification is available. Option D best protects patient safety.
questions.source_name: American Nurses Association — Questions to Ask in the Decision to Accept Assignments
questions.source_detail: ANA advises assessing expertise for float assignments, cross-training and buddy support, and using supervision or assignment modification when experience or knowledge is limited.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of the Incident Command System during a hospital response to a large or complex emergency?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"To replace all standing hospital policies permanently with a disaster chain of command that remains active after the emergency response has ended.","B":"To remove formal command roles so departments can operate independently without shared objectives, common terminology, or coordinated resource management.","C":"To limit incident management to police and fire agencies because healthcare organizations do not use standardized incident-management structures.","D":"To provide a standardized and scalable structure for command, coordination, resources, personnel, facilities, and communication during the incident."}}
questions.rationale: FEMA describes ICS as a standardized approach to command, control, and coordination that integrates personnel, equipment, facilities, procedures, and communications. It is flexible and scalable for incidents of different sizes and is used beyond law enforcement and fire services.
questions.source_name: FEMA — National Incident Management System / Incident Command System
questions.source_detail: FEMA describes ICS as a standardized approach to on-scene command, control and coordination that integrates procedures, personnel, equipment, facilities and communications within a common structure.

questions.stem: A nurse performing telephone triage receives a caller who wants a definitive diagnosis. What is the nurse's most appropriate role?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Give a definitive diagnosis from the symptom list alone because telephone triage protocols are intended to replace a complete medical evaluation by a clinician.","B":"Use structured assessment, clinical judgment, and decision-support tools to determine the urgency and appropriate level of care, while documenting the encounter.","C":"Avoid documenting the call because telephone triage recommendations are informal and do not become part of the clinical information used for follow-up care.","D":"Follow the written algorithm mechanically without considering clinical judgment, because deviations based on patient-specific information are unsafe in telephone triage."}}
questions.rationale: Telephone triage is professional nursing practice rather than remote medical diagnosis. AAACN emphasizes systematic assessment, critical thinking, clinical judgment, appropriate use of decision-support tools, and documentation. Option B accurately describes that role.
questions.source_name: American Academy of Ambulatory Care Nursing — Telephone Triage as Professional Nursing Practice
questions.source_detail: AAACN describes telephone triage as full-scope professional nursing requiring structured assessment, critical thinking, clinical judgment, decision-support tools, and documentation.

questions.stem: A client wants another medical opinion before proceeding with a major elective operation. Which nursing response is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Discourage another opinion because requesting one indicates loss of trust and may justify ending the current therapeutic relationship before surgery is scheduled.","B":"Tell the client that second opinions are reserved for situations in which the treating clinician formally requests consultation from another specialist.","C":"Support the client's decision to seek a second opinion and help clarify how records or referrals can be obtained, while noting possible health-plan requirements.","D":"Advise the client to proceed with the planned operation first because obtaining a second opinion after treatment avoids unnecessary delay in the current plan."}}
questions.rationale: AMA ethics guidance recognizes the patient's ability to seek a second opinion. Option C supports autonomy and practical coordination without implying that all insurance plans cover the same services or that a second opinion is mandatory.
questions.source_name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics — Consultation, Referral & Second Opinions
questions.source_detail: AMA ethics guidance states that patients may seek a second opinion and physicians should assure patients of that option while noting applicable health-plan restrictions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a durable power of attorney for health care?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It authorizes the named agent to manage the person's financial accounts but does not provide authority to participate in medical decision-making if capacity is lost.","B":"It names a health care proxy who can make health care decisions if the person cannot communicate or decide, subject to the document and applicable state law.","C":"It is a physician DNR order specifying which resuscitation measures should be withheld if cardiac or respiratory arrest occurs during an emergency.","D":"It transfers all legal decision-making authority immediately after signing, even while the person retains decision-making capacity and can communicate preferences."}}
questions.rationale: A durable power of attorney for health care names a health care proxy who can make health care decisions if the person cannot communicate or make them. Option B is correct; the document is distinct from financial power of attorney and from a DNR order, and state rules vary.
questions.source_name: National Institute on Aging — Advance Care Planning: Advance Directives for Health Care
questions.source_detail: NIA explains that a durable power of attorney for health care names a health care proxy who can make health care decisions if the person cannot communicate their own wishes; state rules vary.

questions.stem: A client has a do-not-resuscitate (DNR) order. Which statement correctly explains its scope?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The order means routine medications, nutrition, symptom treatment, and nursing care should be stopped because the client has declined further medical treatment.","B":"The order means the client should receive comfort measures only and cannot receive disease-directed treatment even when that treatment remains consistent with goals.","C":"The order directs clinicians not to perform CPR if breathing or heartbeat stops; it does not by itself instruct them to withhold other treatments or pain medicine.","D":"The order applies only to chest compressions, while defibrillation, emergency ventilation, and resuscitation drugs should still be provided during cardiac arrest."}}
questions.rationale: A DNR is specific to cardiopulmonary resuscitation when breathing or heartbeat stops. It does not by itself discontinue medications, nutrition, pain treatment, or other care. Option C accurately states its scope.
questions.source_name: MedlinePlus — Do-not-resuscitate order
questions.source_detail: MedlinePlus states that a DNR instructs providers not to perform CPR if breathing or heartbeat stops and is specific to CPR, not other treatments such as pain medicine or nutrition.

questions.stem: An incapacitated client has a court-appointed guardian whose order expressly includes authority for routine health care decisions. A sibling demands to decide instead. What should the nurse do?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Direct routine health care decisions to the legally authorized guardian within the scope of the court order, while involving the client as much as remaining capacity allows.","B":"Accept the sibling as decision-maker because frequent family involvement automatically overrides authority formally granted to a court-appointed guardian for health care decisions.","C":"Ignore the guardianship order because court-appointed guardians can address placement or finances but can never be authorized to participate in medical decisions.","D":"Ask whichever relative is physically present to decide because legal authority is unnecessary once a client has been documented as lacking decision-making capacity."}}
questions.rationale: Because the scenario expressly states that the court order grants the guardian authority for routine health care decisions, the nurse should direct those decisions to that legally authorized guardian within the order's scope while involving the client to the extent possible. Authority varies by state and court order.
questions.source_name: NIH/PubMed — Medical decision-making during the guardianship process for incapacitated, hospitalized adults
questions.source_detail: Published evidence describes court-appointed guardians acting as legally authorized surrogate decision-makers for incapacitated adults; the extent of authority depends on the court order and state law.

questions.stem: A nurse manager is developing staffing for critically ill patients. Which principle is most consistent with current critical-care staffing standards?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Critically ill patients generally require about one nurse for every one to two patients, with assignments adjusted for acuity, workload, care needs, and nurse competency.","B":"Critical-care assignments should routinely use the same patient load as a general medical-surgical unit because monitoring technology offsets the higher patient acuity.","C":"Every critically ill patient requires permanent one-to-one nursing regardless of acuity, stability, therapies, workload, or the competency and current experience of available nursing staff.","D":"A fixed national ratio alone determines every assignment, so patient condition, workload, care complexity, and nurse competency should not modify staffing decisions."}}
questions.rationale: AACN critical-care staffing standards anticipate that critically ill patients generally require about one nurse for every two patients, with assignment decisions also reflecting acuity, workload, and nurse competency. Option A captures both the baseline and the need for individualized staffing.
questions.source_name: American Association of Critical-Care Nurses — Critical Care Staffing Standards
questions.source_detail: AACN states that critically ill or injured patients generally require about one nurse to two patients, with staffing also matching patient needs and nurse competencies.

questions.stem: A client is diagnosed with acute compartment syndrome of the lower leg. Which treatment should the nurse anticipate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Elevation alone above heart level until swelling resolves because acute compartment syndrome generally improves without surgical pressure release when perfusion is reduced.","B":"Urgent surgical decompression with fasciotomy to relieve compartment pressure and reduce the risk of irreversible nerve and muscle injury from prolonged ischemia.","C":"A tighter circumferential cast to reduce edema because increasing external pressure restores capillary perfusion within the affected muscle compartment during the emergency.","D":"Observe and give oral analgesics until pain resolves because definitive surgery is reserved for chronic exertional compartment syndrome, not acute cases."}}
questions.rationale: Acute compartment syndrome is a surgical emergency. Fasciotomy releases the fascia and relieves dangerous compartment pressure before prolonged ischemia causes irreversible nerve and muscle damage. Option B is correct.
questions.source_name: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons — Acute Compartment Syndrome
questions.source_detail: AAOS identifies acute compartment syndrome as a surgical emergency requiring rapid pressure relief; surgical incisions through skin and fascia relieve dangerous compartment pressure.

questions.stem: A client with diabetic ketoacidosis has a serum potassium concentration of 3.0 mmol/L before insulin is started. Which treatment sequence is expected?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Begin intravenous insulin immediately without potassium replacement because insulin will raise extracellular potassium as ketoacidosis begins to resolve during treatment.","B":"Give a potassium-wasting diuretic before insulin because lowering potassium further reduces the risk of arrhythmia when glucose enters cells during DKA therapy.","C":"Withhold fluids and potassium until insulin normalizes glucose because electrolyte replacement before glycemic correction increases the risk of cerebral edema.","D":"Begin potassium replacement and delay insulin until potassium rises above 3.5 mmol/L, because insulin can lower serum potassium further and provoke serious arrhythmias."}}
questions.rationale: With DKA and potassium below 3.5 mmol/L, current consensus guidance recommends potassium replacement and delaying insulin until potassium exceeds 3.5 mmol/L. Starting insulin at 3.0 mmol/L can worsen hypokalemia and precipitate life-threatening arrhythmias or respiratory muscle weakness.
questions.source_name: ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS — Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report
questions.source_detail: The 2024 consensus report recommends potassium replacement when admission potassium is below 3.5 mmol/L and delaying insulin until potassium rises above 3.5 mmol/L.

questions.stem: Which finding most strongly favors serotonin syndrome over neuroleptic malignant syndrome in a client with hyperthermia and altered mental status?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Generalized bradyreflexia with marked lead-pipe rigidity developing over several days after exposure to a dopamine-blocking medication used for psychosis.","B":"Hyperreflexia and inducible or spontaneous clonus developing rapidly after exposure to a serotonergic medication or a clinically important medication change.","C":"Profound flaccid paralysis without tremor, clonus, hyperreflexia, or rigidity after a medication change involving both serotonergic and antipsychotic agents.","D":"Isolated fever without neuromuscular abnormalities because serotonin syndrome is distinguished from NMS mainly by the absence of abnormal reflexes or muscle activity."}}
questions.rationale: Serotonin syndrome usually has neuromuscular hyperreactivity, especially hyperreflexia and clonus, and often develops rapidly after a serotonergic exposure or change. NMS more often features marked rigidity and a slower onset. Option B is the best discriminator.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Serotonin Syndrome
questions.source_detail: Serotonin syndrome is characterized by neuromuscular hyperreactivity including hyperreflexia and clonus, whereas NMS more typically produces a slowed neuromuscular response with rigidity.

questions.stem: After treatment for anaphylaxis, the client's symptoms have fully resolved. Why may continued observation still be appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Anaphylaxis can recur as a biphasic reaction after initial resolution, so observation should be individualized according to episode severity, treatment needs, and risk factors.","B":"Every patient must remain hospitalized for the same fixed period because biphasic reactions occur at a predictable time regardless of episode severity or treatment response.","C":"Recurrence is possible only after another exposure to the allergen, so observation is unnecessary once symptoms resolve if the trigger has been removed from the environment.","D":"Observation is needed mainly to confirm that epinephrine has been eliminated because residual epinephrine itself commonly causes a second anaphylactic episode after clinical recovery."}}
questions.rationale: A biphasic anaphylactic reaction can occur after apparent initial resolution. Continued observation can therefore be appropriate, but the duration should be individualized rather than assumed to be identical for every patient. Option A reflects current risk-based practice.
questions.source_name: AAAAI — Anaphylaxis
questions.source_detail: AAAAI notes that anaphylaxis symptoms can resolve and later return, and recommends emergency evaluation and monitoring after anaphylaxis; observation is individualized according to clinical course and risk.

questions.stem: A client exercising in extreme heat has a core temperature of 40.5°C (104.9°F), confusion, and hot skin. Which condition should the nurse suspect?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Heat exhaustion, because altered mental status with a temperature above 40°C is typical of a mild heat illness that responds to oral fluids alone.","B":"Heat stroke, a life-threatening emergency characterized by severe hyperthermia with central nervous system dysfunction and requiring rapid cooling.","C":"Simple dehydration, because confusion during exercise is expected when fluid intake has been inadequate and does not require emergency cooling measures.","D":"A normal physiologic response to strenuous activity, because very high core temperature and confusion commonly occur during intense exercise without heat injury."}}
questions.rationale: Heat stroke is a life-threatening heat illness characterized by marked hyperthermia with central nervous system dysfunction such as confusion. Rapid cooling and emergency medical care are required. Option B is correct; sweating may be absent or present, especially in exertional heat stroke.
questions.source_name: CDC/NIOSH — Heat-related Illnesses
questions.source_detail: CDC identifies heat stroke by very high body temperature and central nervous system dysfunction such as confusion and recommends immediate emergency care and rapid cooling.

questions.stem: A client exposed to cold has a core temperature of 31°C (87.8°F), confusion, and slowed responses. Which management principle is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Treat this as mild cold stress and encourage vigorous walking because active exercise is the preferred way to restore core temperature in confused patients.","B":"Handle the client carefully, prevent further heat loss, apply active rewarming focused on the trunk, and monitor for dysrhythmias during transport and treatment.","C":"Immerse the entire client immediately in very hot water because rapid peripheral heating is the safest first-line method for moderate hypothermia in adults.","D":"Massage the arms and legs vigorously to increase peripheral circulation because moving cold blood back to the core decreases the risk of ventricular dysrhythmias."}}
questions.rationale: At about 31°C with mental-status change, the client has clinically significant hypothermia requiring careful handling, prevention of further heat loss, active rewarming directed toward the trunk, and cardiac monitoring. The prior rationale was corrected: current wilderness guidance does not support a blanket rule of deliberately slow rewarming to prevent a presumed 'rewarming shock.'
questions.source_name: Wilderness Medical Society — Clinical Practice Guidelines for Accidental Hypothermia
questions.source_detail: WMS guidance emphasizes careful handling, protection from further heat loss, active external rewarming focused on the trunk, and awareness of ventricular dysrhythmia risk in moderate/severe hypothermia.

questions.stem: A client with frostbitten fingers arrives for care. Which rewarming method is appropriate when refreezing can be prevented?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Rapidly rewarm the affected fingers in circulating water maintained at about 37–39°C (98.6–102.2°F), then protect the rewarmed tissue from refreezing and further trauma.","B":"Massage the frozen fingers vigorously during rewarming because friction improves tissue perfusion and reduces microvascular injury after prolonged freezing and cold exposure.","C":"Apply direct dry heat from a heating pad or heater because numb frostbitten tissue requires a hotter source than water to achieve adequate tissue rewarming.","D":"Allow the fingers to thaw slowly at room temperature even when a controlled warm-water bath is available, because slow rewarming produces better tissue outcomes."}}
questions.rationale: WMS recommends rapid water-bath rewarming at 37–39°C when thawing can be maintained. Rubbing and direct dry heat can worsen tissue injury, and refreezing after thawing is especially harmful. Option A is correct.
questions.source_name: Wilderness Medical Society — Frostbite Clinical Practice Guideline Summary 2024
questions.source_detail: WMS recommends rapid rewarming in water maintained at 37–39°C, avoiding rubbing and direct heat, and protecting thawed tissue from refreezing and trauma.

questions.stem: An alert adult was rescued from a drowning event and now has normal breathing, mentation, and oxygenation in the emergency department. Which statement is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The client can develop 'secondary drowning' without warning several days later despite remaining normal, so prolonged hospitalization is routinely required.","B":"Terms such as 'secondary' or 'dry' drowning are not medically accepted; an initially well survivor may be observed for several hours and discharged if still normal.","C":"Any new cough or breathing problem days later should automatically be attributed to delayed drowning, even if the client had been completely asymptomatic after rescue.","D":"If spontaneous breathing returns at the scene, no emergency assessment or observation is useful because clinically important respiratory deterioration cannot occur afterward."}}
questions.rationale: The terms 'secondary drowning,' 'delayed drowning,' 'dry drowning,' and 'near-drowning' are not medically accepted. An alert drowning survivor who becomes completely normal may be observed for several hours; if still normal, discharge can be appropriate. Clinically important deterioration occurs with preceding symptoms rather than an unexpected death days later after complete recovery.
questions.source_name: American Red Cross — Debunking Dry or Delayed/Secondary Drowning
questions.source_detail: The Red Cross states that 'secondary,' 'delayed,' 'dry,' and 'near-drowning' are not accepted diagnoses and describes observation for initially well survivors rather than prolonged admission for a mythical delayed syndrome.

questions.stem: A medication requires conventional peak-and-trough therapeutic drug monitoring. When should a trough concentration generally be obtained?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Immediately after the dose is administered, when the serum concentration is expected to be near its highest point in the dosing interval.","B":"At a random midpoint between doses because trough interpretation does not depend on the timing of the specimen relative to medication administration.","C":"Near the end of the dosing interval, immediately before the next scheduled dose, when the serum drug concentration is expected to be lowest.","D":"Only after the medication has been permanently discontinued because trough values measured during ongoing therapy cannot guide dosing or toxicity assessment."}}
questions.rationale: A trough concentration represents the low point of a dosing interval and is generally obtained immediately before the next scheduled dose. Timing must be interpreted according to the specific medication and monitoring protocol. Option C is correct.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Nursing Pharmacology: Peak and Trough Levels
questions.source_detail: NCBI Nursing Pharmacology defines a trough as the lowest drug concentration and states that it is drawn right before the next scheduled dose.

questions.stem: A client with diabetes has hyperglycemia, ketones, metabolic acidosis, and an elevated anion gap. How should the nurse interpret the elevated anion gap?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It supports the presence of high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis from accumulated unmeasured acids, although ketone measurement is more direct for assessing DKA.","B":"It establishes metabolic alkalosis because an increased anion gap reflects excess bicarbonate rather than accumulation of ketoacids or other unmeasured acids.","C":"It proves that the acidosis is respiratory in origin because anion-gap calculations are used primarily to classify abnormalities in carbon dioxide elimination.","D":"It independently confirms that DKA has resolved because a persistently elevated anion gap is expected after ketones and acid-base abnormalities normalize."}}
questions.rationale: An elevated anion gap supports high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis from accumulated unmeasured acids such as ketoacids. Current DKA guidance favors direct beta-hydroxybutyrate measurement when available and cautions against using the anion gap alone as a resolution criterion. Option A preserves that distinction.
questions.source_name: ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS — Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report
questions.source_detail: The 2024 consensus report describes DKA as ketone-related metabolic acidosis and recommends direct beta-hydroxybutyrate assessment when available rather than relying on the anion gap alone.

questions.stem: A dehydrated client with glucose 650 mg/dL has markedly elevated effective serum osmolality and altered mental status. Which condition is most consistent with these findings?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A hypotonic state caused by water excess, because severe hyperglycemia lowers effective serum osmolality and commonly produces dilutional cerebral edema.","B":"Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state, in which severe hyperglycemia and osmotic diuresis produce profound dehydration and elevated effective serum osmolality.","C":"Isolated hypoglycemia, because altered mental status with high measured glucose indicates that circulating glucose is unavailable to the central nervous system.","D":"Uncomplicated fasting ketosis, because serum glucose above 600 mg/dL with marked hyperosmolality is expected during normal adaptation to reduced carbohydrate intake."}}
questions.rationale: HHS is characterized by severe hyperglycemia, hyperosmolality, and substantial dehydration from osmotic diuresis, often with altered cognition. Option B matches the described pattern; diagnostic interpretation should use the full laboratory and clinical criteria.
questions.source_name: ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS — Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report
questions.source_detail: The 2024 consensus report defines HHS by severe hyperglycemia and hyperosmolality with dehydration and little or no significant ketoacidosis, and discusses neurologic manifestations with increasing osmolality.

questions.stem: A client with a mechanical mitral valve replacement is receiving warfarin. Which INR target is recommended by the ACC/AHA valve guideline?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A target INR of 1.0, because mechanical mitral prostheses do not require therapeutic anticoagulation after the early initial postoperative period.","B":"A target INR of 3.0, reflecting the thrombogenic risk of a mechanical mitral valve; INR targets differ for other mechanical valves and risk profiles.","C":"A target INR of 1.5 for every mechanical valve, because the same low-intensity anticoagulation target applies regardless of valve type, position, or risk factors.","D":"No INR target, because direct oral anticoagulants are preferred over vitamin K antagonists for routine anticoagulation in clients with mechanical mitral valves."}}
questions.rationale: ACC/AHA guidance specifies an INR target of 3.0 for mechanical mitral valve replacement. The original item was overgeneralized because mechanical-valve INR targets differ by valve position, prosthesis type, and thromboembolic risk; for example, some mechanical aortic valves use different targets. Option B is specific and correct.
questions.source_name: American College of Cardiology — 2020 ACC/AHA Heart Valve Disease Guideline: Key Perspectives, Part 3
questions.source_detail: ACC/AHA guidance specifies INR 3.0 for mechanical mitral valve replacement and different targets for several mechanical aortic-valve scenarios.

questions.stem: A client's BUN rises disproportionately more than creatinine during an illness with volume loss and reduced renal perfusion. What does this pattern suggest?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It can support a prerenal pattern such as dehydration or reduced renal perfusion, but the ratio should be interpreted with the clinical picture and other data.","B":"It specifically proves postrenal obstruction because a high BUN-to-creatinine ratio uniquely identifies blocked urinary outflow regardless of the patient's volume status.","C":"It demonstrates improved glomerular filtration because BUN rises relative to creatinine when renal clearance becomes more efficient during volume depletion.","D":"It is diagnostically meaningless because BUN and creatinine are unrelated to renal perfusion and cannot contribute to assessment of prerenal azotemia."}}
questions.rationale: A disproportionately high BUN relative to creatinine can support a prerenal pattern, particularly with volume depletion or reduced perfusion. It is a clue rather than a stand-alone diagnosis because BUN is influenced by multiple nonrenal factors. Option A correctly preserves that limitation.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Prerenal Kidney Failure
questions.source_detail: NCBI describes a BUN-to-creatinine ratio above about 20:1 as a common prerenal pattern while emphasizing clinical evaluation and the limitations of laboratory markers.

questions.stem: A critically ill adult has a measured cardiac output of 2.1 L/min at rest. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"This is above the expected resting range because normal adult cardiac output is generally less than 1 L/min when metabolic demand is low in a healthy person.","B":"This is below the usual resting adult range of about 4–8 L/min and should be interpreted with body size, cardiac index, perfusion findings, and clinical context.","C":"This is within the expected resting range because normal cardiac output is approximately 2 L/min regardless of body size, heart rate, or stroke volume.","D":"This is normal only during exercise because adult cardiac output typically falls to about 2 L/min with exertion and rises toward 20–30 L/min during sleep and rest."}}
questions.rationale: Resting adult cardiac output is generally about 4–8 L/min, with an average near 5 L/min, but body size and physiologic state matter. A measured 2.1 L/min is below that usual range and should be interpreted with cardiac index and perfusion findings. Option B is correct.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Physiology, Cardiac Index
questions.source_detail: NCBI states that resting cardiac output generally falls between 4 and 8 L/min and averages around 5 L/min; cardiac index normalizes output for body surface area.

questions.stem: A nurse is suctioning an adult client through an artificial airway. Which technique is consistent with current AARC guidance?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Apply suction continuously while advancing the catheter deeply until resistance is met, because deep suctioning is preferred for routine secretion removal.","B":"Preoxygenate as indicated, use sterile technique for open suctioning, and limit each suction application to no more than about 15 seconds during the procedure.","C":"Instill normal saline routinely before every suction pass because lavage improves secretion clearance and is recommended for all artificial-airway suctioning.","D":"Use scheduled deep suctioning even without clinical indications because routine suctioning prevents secretion retention more effectively than as-needed assessment."}}
questions.rationale: The 2022 AARC guideline recommends preoxygenation for adult and pediatric artificial-airway suctioning, sterile technique for open suctioning, avoidance of routine normal saline instillation, and a maximum suction application of 15 seconds. Deep suctioning is reserved for situations in which shallow suctioning is ineffective. Option B is correct.
questions.source_name: AARC — Clinical Practice Guidelines: Artificial Airway Suctioning (2022)
questions.source_detail: AARC recommends preoxygenation, sterile technique for open suctioning, generally avoiding normal saline, limiting suction application to a maximum of 15 seconds, and using deep suctioning only when shallow suctioning is ineffective.

questions.stem: Which action is appropriate when caring for a client with a chest tube connected to a drainage system?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Place the drainage system on the bed beside the client so the tubing remains level with the chest and gravity does not increase pleural drainage.","B":"Keep the drainage system upright and below the client's chest to promote drainage and reduce the risk of fluid flowing back toward the pleural space.","C":"Raise the drainage system above the chest during repositioning because temporary elevation prevents excessive negative pressure and protects the lung from injury.","D":"Clamp the chest tube routinely during transport because an open drainage pathway increases the risk of pneumothorax whenever wall suction is disconnected."}}
questions.rationale: A chest drainage system should remain upright and below the chest or insertion site to facilitate drainage and prevent fluid from flowing backward toward the pleural space. Routine elevation above the chest or unnecessary clamping can create hazards. Option B is correct.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Care of a Chest Tube
questions.source_detail: Current chest-tube guidance states that the drainage system should be upright and positioned below chest level to facilitate drainage and prevent fluid or air backflow.

questions.stem: Which intervention is most important for maintaining an indwelling urinary catheter drainage system and reducing CAUTI risk?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Disconnect the catheter from the collection tubing once per shift so the tubing can be rinsed and inspected before the closed system is reassembled.","B":"Rest the collection bag on the floor when the client is in bed because this keeps the bag below the bladder and improves dependent drainage.","C":"Maintain a closed drainage system, keep the tubing free of kinks, and keep the collection bag below bladder level without allowing it to touch the floor.","D":"Replace the catheter and drainage bag at fixed daily intervals even when the system remains intact because routine replacement reduces bacterial colonization."}}
questions.rationale: CDC CAUTI guidance recommends maintaining a closed drainage system and unobstructed urine flow, keeping tubing free of kinks, and keeping the collection bag below bladder level without placing it on the floor. Routine fixed-interval replacement is not recommended. Option C is correct.
questions.source_name: CDC — CAUTI Summary of Recommendations
questions.source_detail: CDC recommends a closed drainage system, unobstructed urine flow, kink-free tubing, and a collection bag below bladder level that does not rest on the floor.

questions.stem: When performing an aseptic wound-care procedure involving sites with different contamination levels, which sequencing principle is appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Move repeatedly from the most contaminated area back to the least contaminated area so the same supplies distribute cleansing solution evenly throughout the wound.","B":"Begin with the most contaminated portion because organisms should be loosened first before cleaner tissue is handled with the same instruments and materials.","C":"Clean all areas in random order because contamination level does not affect aseptic sequencing as long as sterile gloves are worn throughout the procedure.","D":"Work from the least contaminated area toward the more contaminated area, using technique and supplies that prevent carrying organisms back toward cleaner tissue."}}
questions.rationale: General aseptic sequencing follows a clean-to-dirty principle, moving from the least contaminated toward the more contaminated sites while avoiding transfer back to cleaner areas. Wound irrigation should also use enough pressure to cleanse without traumatizing tissue or driving organisms deeper. Option D is correct.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Nursing Skills: Aseptic Technique and Wound Care
questions.source_detail: NCBI Nursing Skills states that aseptic procedures generally proceed from clean to dirty, working from least to most contaminated sites and parts; wound irrigation should cleanse without driving bacteria deeper.

questions.stem: Which statement about human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"HPV vaccination treats established HPV infection and removes existing precancerous lesions, so it is primarily used after abnormal screening results are confirmed.","B":"HPV vaccination prevents new infections with vaccine HPV types and helps prevent multiple HPV-associated cancers as well as most genital warts before exposure.","C":"HPV vaccination is recommended only after sexual activity begins because prior exposure is needed for the vaccine to generate protective immunity against HPV.","D":"HPV vaccination eliminates the need for recommended cervical cancer screening because vaccinated people cannot develop infection from any cancer-associated HPV type."}}
questions.rationale: HPV vaccination prevents new HPV infections and protects against HPV types responsible for most HPV-associated cancers and most genital warts; it does not treat established infection or remove existing lesions. It works best before exposure. Option B is correct.
questions.source_name: CDC — Preventing HPV-Associated Cancers / HPV Vaccine Recommendations
questions.source_detail: CDC states that HPV vaccination prevents new HPV infections, protects against HPV types causing most HPV-associated cancers and most genital warts, and works best before exposure.

questions.stem: An asymptomatic 45-year-old adult is at average risk for colorectal cancer and has never been screened. What does the USPSTF recommend?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Defer screening until age 60 because colorectal cancer screening before that age has no demonstrated net benefit for average-risk asymptomatic adults.","B":"Screen only if gastrointestinal symptoms develop because screening recommendations do not apply to adults who have no signs or symptoms of colorectal cancer.","C":"Begin colorectal cancer screening now; the USPSTF recommends screening average-risk adults starting at age 45 through age 75 using an appropriate strategy.","D":"Perform colonoscopy every year because annual colonoscopy is the preferred USPSTF screening schedule for all average-risk adults beginning at age 45."}}
questions.rationale: The USPSTF recommends colorectal cancer screening for average-risk asymptomatic adults beginning at age 45. Multiple acceptable strategies exist; annual colonoscopy is not the recommended schedule. Option C is correct.
questions.source_name: USPSTF — Colorectal Cancer: Screening
questions.source_detail: USPSTF recommends screening average-risk asymptomatic adults beginning at age 45, with Grade B for ages 45–49 and Grade A for ages 50–75.

questions.stem: A woman of reproductive age screens positive for intimate partner violence and is not in immediate danger. Which follow-up is most consistent with the 2025 USPSTF evidence?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Provide only a telephone number and end the encounter because brief referral information alone is the evidence-based intervention shown to improve IPV outcomes.","B":"Require immediate separation from the partner because clinicians should determine the safest living arrangement regardless of the patient's preferences or circumstances.","C":"Offer or refer her to a multicomponent intervention with ongoing support, address safety and resources privately, and respect her autonomy in shared decision-making.","D":"Avoid further discussion unless physical injuries are visible because screening-positive patients without acute injury do not benefit from support or referral services."}}
questions.rationale: The 2025 USPSTF recommendation finds benefit when women of reproductive age who screen positive for IPV are provided or referred to evidence-based multicomponent interventions with ongoing support. A single brief referral alone is not equivalent to the supported intervention. Safety assessment should be private and care should respect patient autonomy. Option C is correct.
questions.source_name: USPSTF — Intimate Partner Violence and Caregiver Abuse: Screening (2025)
questions.source_detail: USPSTF recommends IPV screening for women of reproductive age and providing or referring those who screen positive to multicomponent interventions with ongoing support.

questions.stem: An adult's spouse died 14 months ago. The client has persistent intense longing, preoccupation with the death, and major impairment in daily functioning. Which condition should be evaluated?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Normal uncomplicated grief only, because grief-related impairment cannot represent a diagnosable condition regardless of duration, severity, or effect on functioning.","B":"Prolonged grief disorder, while assessing the full DSM-5-TR criteria and considering cultural context, other psychiatric conditions, and functional impairment.","C":"Acute stress disorder, because symptoms more than a year after bereavement are classified as an acute trauma response rather than a grief disorder.","D":"A manic episode, because persistent yearning and preoccupation after bereavement are characteristic signs of elevated mood and increased goal-directed activity."}}
questions.rationale: For adults, prolonged grief disorder requires that the death occurred at least 12 months earlier and involves persistent intense grief symptoms with clinically significant distress or functional impairment; the full DSM-5-TR criteria and cultural context must still be assessed. Option B is the appropriate condition to evaluate, not an automatic diagnosis based on duration alone.
questions.source_name: American Psychiatric Association — Prolonged Grief Disorder
questions.source_detail: APA describes prolonged grief disorder as intense, persistent grief associated with functional impairment and notes that for adults the death must have occurred at least one year earlier before the diagnosis can be made.

questions.stem: Which nursing action best illustrates therapeutic use of self in a mental health setting?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Share extensive personal experiences whenever the client is distressed so the conversation focuses on the nurse's history and creates a friendship outside clinical boundaries.","B":"Remain emotionally detached and avoid self-awareness because the nurse's personality, reactions, and relational style should never influence therapeutic interactions.","C":"Use self-awareness, presence, communication, empathy, and professional boundaries intentionally to build trust and support the client's therapeutic goals and recovery.","D":"Adopt the client's beliefs without reflection because agreement is necessary for rapport and is more important than maintaining professional judgment or boundaries."}}
questions.rationale: Therapeutic use of self is intentional, reflective, ethically bounded use of the nurse's professional self to foster trust and therapeutic outcomes. It depends on self-awareness, relational presence, communication, empathy, and professional boundaries rather than unfiltered self-disclosure or detachment. Option C is correct.
questions.source_name: NIH/PubMed — The Therapeutic Use of Self by Mental Health Nurses: An Evolving Practice (2026)
questions.source_detail: Current mental-health nursing literature describes therapeutic use of self as intentional and reflective use of the professional self to foster connection, presence, trust, and therapeutic outcomes while maintaining ethical boundaries.
